findings.summary: `setPbrSkybox` and `setPbrUnlit` shared one case, and the loaded-container stamp at the end of it tested only that the material came from a container -- not which setter was being lowered -- so a skybox setter on a loaded material would have recorded the container's UNLIT fact and composed every material of that document unlit. The two cases are split; the four lines they shared are boilerplate every neighbouring case repeats anyway

the whole-mesh-list precondition three doc comments asserted was enforced nowhere: the licence rode on `mesh.material` carrying its owner's asset, and `readProperty` attaches that for ANY asset-mesh collection, so a bound `getContainerMeshes` result or `container.meshes ?? []` -- neither proving the loop reaches everything -- could stamp a whole document. The licence is now minted by the proven loop itself as `assetWholeMeshList`, and the unproven routes refuse

assets are keyed by source, so two `loadGltf` calls on one URL share a record -- scene 73's exact shape -- and a container-level fact stamped from one would have composed the other's materials unlit. `loadGltf` counts the containers a record backs and the stamp refuses above one

`HandleCollectionTarget` had become a field-for-field twin of `HandleCollectionInfo`, so both places that widened one into the other were identity functions written out longhand; it is an alias now and they are one-line returns

the favicon route was at the wrong layer AND cost more than it saved: two of the three servers answer every path with their shell page and never 404, while the suite server did not merely log -- `/favicon.ico` fell through to a live raw.githubusercontent.com fetch, so every capture paid a round trip to be told the lab has no favicon either. A Playwright route also disables the page cache and adds a browser-to-Node hop per request, measured at +21% (637ms -> 769ms) on scene229's 538-request load. It is three lines in the server that owns the policy

the proof's guard chains were written as `const x = y && unwrap(y)` followed by re-testing both halves, six times, twice evaluating the same type predicate in both the initializer and the guard; as early returns they say the same thing in half the lines

three places hand-rolled "unwrap, is it an identifier, does its text match"; `isIdentifierRead` names it, and the sibling walk proof beside it -- which spelled out both that check and the property read, with a cast -- now calls both helpers instead of its own copies

`isImportedMeshFlattenWalk` returned the container parameter and documented doing so, but its one caller used it as a predicate and nothing outside the module imported it; it answers a boolean and is no longer exported

the tint's static-Color3 check was a fifth copy of a shape `setPbrEmissive` spells out a hundred lines up in the same switch; `requiredStaticColor3` beside the existing `requiredStaticFiniteNumber` serves both, so the two setters can no longer drift in what they accept
the new `for...of` arm was the existing handle-collection arm re-typed -- same resolve, same binding refusal, same loop; `emitCollectionForOfBody` holds that tail once and only the licence differs
the per-asset options bag stopped one fact short: `selectedVariant` stayed spread identically at all three variant-composer calls, one of them inside a loop. `assetVariantOptions` carries it
`recordAssetSceneUnlit`'s three-arm `same` plus its `if (!same)` double negative restate one comparison of two optional tints

the new forwarder in compiler.ts was spliced between an existing doc comment and the method it documented, leaving the comment describing the wrong method and `assetRootChildrenIterationTarget` undocumented

docs/features.md and the proof's own comment claimed the walk is proven to BE the pin's `getContainerMeshes`. It is not: the pin tests `_gpu` for truth where this tests both renderable fields for presence, and keeps a `seen` set this has no need of. Both now say what is actually proven -- the reach and the selection, never the order

a ~200-line structural recognizer had no test of its own; the scene gate was the only thing exercising it, and nothing at all covered the refusals. Four tests cover the emission, a walk whose renderable test is not the walk's, the unlicensed `getContainerMeshes` route, and the twice-loaded asset

the speculative `for...of` probe was checked for cost rather than assumed: of 292 corpus `for...of` statements, 284 bail at `ts.isCallExpression` and the remaining 8 bail on the 4-statement body check before any symbol resolution, with `compileValue` reached only after the walk is fully proven -- stricter than the neighbouring `assetRootChildrenIterationTarget`, which compiles the owner of any `.children` loop
findings.blockedBy: Nothing to apply: the measurement confirmed the ordering already puts every cheap syntactic check ahead of the expensive ones.
findings.filedIn: Recorded here; docs/features.md describes the walk's acceptance and no TODO entry is warranted for a measurement that found no cost.

findings.summary: the flatten walk appears in a recursive-closure spelling too (scene 73) that the worklist proof does not accept, and the deeper answer the altitude angle names -- evaluating the helper over the document's node tree at generation and comparing the returned set to the loader's mesh list, which would accept any pure spelling -- is a larger capability than this scene needs
findings.blockedBy: The generation-time evaluation needs a mesh-member list on the asset collection that does not exist yet; `collectionMembers` builds that shape for animation groups only, and no measured scene reaches the recursive spelling without also being blocked earlier (scene 73 stops at camera viewports first).
